subject: Account foundation checklist — LumaCare private deployment
messages:
From: Jonas Reece <infra-eng@lumacare.com>

Cc: ops_lead@lumacare.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Account foundation checklist for private deployment kickoff

Sean —

Thanks again for the kickoff today. As discussed, we want to accelerate the VPC/on-prem handoff for the private deployment and land the minimal "account foundation" items so your runtime team can start smoke tests next week. I've attached our current network inventory and a sketch of the topology we plan to provide.

Quick checklist from our side (questions inline):
- Service account(s): we plan to create a read/write deployment SA and a separate operator SA for rollout tasks — do you have naming/role conventions you require?
- Interconnect / tunnel: we'll provision a dedicated VPN tunnel (IPSec) and have the cloud peer IPs ready on 4/23 — any MTU or keepalive settings you recommend?
- Firewall rules: we'll open the minimal set of CIDR ranges you give us. Can you confirm port and protocol list?
- TLS / certs: will Redwood accept customer-supplied certs for internal endpoints or do you require public certs?
- KMS / keywrap: we can either bring our vault or let you manage a CMK — what's simplest for the first pass?

Attachments: lumacare-network-inventory.csv, vpc-topology-draft.pdf

If you can send your "account foundation" checklist back with the items that are blockers vs. can-wait, that'd help us prioritize.

Cheers,
Jonas Reece
Infra Engineer, LumaCare
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Account foundation checklist for private deployment kickoff

Jonas —

Thanks for the inventory and topology. Below is the account foundation checklist from Redwood's side. I've marked each item as REQUIRED (blocker for smoke tests) or RECOMMENDED (can follow). Marissa (runtime) and Karthik (network) are looped for details/follow-through.

Account foundation checklist (Redwood)
- Service accounts + IAM (REQUIRED)
  - One deployment SA with roles: compute.run, storage.objects.readwrite, logging.append. Name convention: rw-deploy-<acct>-<env>. Please share the SA email and a key in an HSM-backed exchange.
- Network peering / routing (REQUIRED)
  - We need a static /30 for tunnel endpoints and explicit route to the tenant VPC. BGP is optional; if using static routes, ensure route priority matches the intended path.
- MTU: 1400 recommended for IPSec with VXLAN.
- Firewall rules (REQUIRED)
  - Allow inbound TLS 443 from Redwood public IP block x.x.33.0/24 to the tenant ingress appliance.
  - Allow outbound NTP (udp/123) and DNS (udp/53) to your resolvers.
- TLS (RECOMMENDED for phase 1)
  - Customer-provided certs are fine for internal endpoints if they chain to a well-known root. For the control plane we require cert pinning; we'll provide CSR if you want us to sign.
- KMS access (REQUIRED)
  - We prefer you provision a CMK with grant to rw-deploy service account OR provide a wrapped DEK. Karthik: we'll need the key ARN and the access policy.
- Service endpoints / egress (REQUIRED)
  - List of outbound endpoints Redwood will call (artifact storage, model registry). We'll whitelist x.x.x.10-20.
- Test accounts + sample payloads (REQUIRED)
  - Please provide a test service account, small S3-compatible bucket with 5 test artifacts, and a short prompt set (3 prompts) for smoke validation.

Attachments referenced: account-foundation-checklist-template.xlsx

Next steps
- Jonas: confirm SA names and KMS approach by EOD 4/21.
- Marissa: prepare runtime smoke test script and minimal telemetry to validate CPU/GPU scheduling.
- Karthik: I'll hand off network checklist items to you; propose we schedule the peering window 4/23 02:00-03:30 PT.

Thanks — quick tech notes and timeline from Runtime/Infra:

Technical clarifications (from Marissa)
- Service account keys: please create a short-lived key for the test SA (24h) and an HSM-wrapped key for production. We will not accept long-lived plaintext keys.
- KMS policy: the grant should allow: Encrypt, Decrypt, GenerateDataKey without CreateKey. Provide the key ARN and the principal (rw-deploy-lumacare-prod).
- Network: we'll run an initial connectivity smoke that includes: TCP 443 TLS handshake, HTTP GET to /healthz, and end-to-end inference invocation (3 sample prompts). We'll provide a small container image (redwood/smoke:2027-04) to run locally if you want to host the probe.
- Time sync: confirm NTP pool or provide an NTP endpoint — clock skew >250ms can break TLS session resumption.

Proposed timeline
- 4/21: LumaCare creates SA(s) + shares HSM wrap/ARN.
- 4/23 02:00-03:30 PT: Tunnel bring-up + routing verification (Karthik to run BGP/static test).
- 4/23 05:00 PT: Runtime smoke tests (Marissa runs tests; results posted to Drive).

I've opened JIRA PDEP-341 for the network handoff and attached the smoke test checklist to the ticket. I'll post the smoke test results and a short runbook to the Drive link once complete.

Attachments: account-foundation-checklist-template.xlsx

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Lead, Runtime Operations, Redwood Inference
